Venture Studio
emerging_asset_class_candidate
Build-not-buy mechanism: the entity co-founds companies internally using shared capital, talent, and operational infrastructure rather than acquiring or investing in externally-originated startups. Distinguishing signal: the studio originates the idea, recruits or co-founds with an operator/CEO, and holds equity from day zero. Venture studios are NOT acquirers (Portfolio Capital), NOT fund investors (LMV), and NOT accelerators that admit external teams (ECOSYSTEM). The mechanism is origination + co-founding + shared-platform scaling.Portfolio-level equity from internally-originated companies; studio fees from corporate partners in some models; fund returns where a parallel fund arm exists.Portfolio company exits (strategic acquisition, PE, IPO), fund distributions, studio fee income.

How the classes differ five mechanism axes

The classes look similar because they share the vocabulary of capital. They separate cleanly on five structural axes — these are the questions that resolve almost every boundary case.

Acquire vs Build vs Fund-external
Portfolio Capital (acquires existing) | Venture Studio (builds in-house) | LMV / UVC (funds external founders)
The line venture studios were hiding behind inside Portfolio Capital - a fundamentally different mechanism.
Equity vs Non-dilutive credit
SMV (RBF, debt, mezz, ABL, factoring, secondaries) | every other class (equity)
Specialty credit slid into Patient and Portfolio on long-hold / balance-sheet language; the instrument test pulls it back to SMV.
Principal vs Agent
All 7 allocator classes (deploy own/LP capital) | Ecosystem layer (advise, broker, convene)
RIAs, OCIOs, brokers, marketplaces, networks and grantmakers wear allocator vocabulary but deploy none of their own capital.
Private vs Public-charter mandate
Sovereign Capital (public legal charter) | every other class (private LP / balance-sheet)
Public pensions and state pools differ from family balance-sheets by the SOURCE of the mandate, not the hold period.
Exit-constrained vs Exit-seeking
Patient Capital (structural no-exit) | most classes (harvest on a horizon) | UVC (unicorn exit - the baseline we exclude)
The original taxonomy conflated 'long hold' with 'patient'; the real test is whether exit is structurally off the table.

Where the classes bleed 155 contested companies, resolved

Classification credibility is the core of this work. Every company below sat on a boundary between two classes. Each is shown with what it looked like, why it was ambiguous, what decided its final class, and — in its own words — the verbatim self-description that settled it. Groups are ordered by how much confusion they caused.

Patient Capital <-> UVC (excluded)50 companies
What it looks like

VC and PE funds wrapped in mission, impact, 'patient', or founder-friendly language.

Why it’s confusing

The vocabulary of capital - 'long-term', 'partner', 'mission-driven' - is shared, so a keyword gate cannot tell a steward from a standard fund.

What decides it

If it raises a standard LP fund with a target IRR and a defined exit cycle, it is classic unicorn-style VC/PE and is excluded as UVC - regardless of the rhetoric.
